technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the landing page within the existing Spring XD web/admin application and reuse its current navigation, templates, styling, and routing conventions.
Implement retryability as configurable exception matching, supporting bus-level defaults and stream-deployment-level overrides, with the more specific stream setting taking precedence.
Use fully qualified exception class names for retry configuration and evaluate the actual exception cause chain so exceptions wrapped by messaging or integration components are handled consistently.
Treat deserialization failures, including Kryo-related failures, as non-retryable by default while allowing explicit configuration where technically safe.

Upgrade Spring Integration, SI Kafka, and Spring Hadoop dependencies in the existing build and retain the project’s current supported Java and dependency-management conventions unless compatibility requires a documented adjustment.
Expose Kafka consumer and producer tuning properties through the existing bus and module deployment property mechanisms rather than introducing a separate configuration system.
Obtain module and container identifiers from the existing runtime/module execution context and expose them through the standard module context or metadata API for logging.
Consolidate XD and XD-plus-Ambari RPM build scripts into one public repository while preserving existing script entry points and build outputs where practical.

Use automated unit, integration, build, and regression tests for retry behavior, configuration precedence, Kafka properties, runtime identifiers, dependency upgrades, web navigation, and RPM packaging.
assumptions: The existing source repositories, build infrastructure, CI configuration, web application, message-bus implementations, and RPM scripts are available and buildable before development begins.
The increment is implemented by one experienced Java/Spring developer who also performs testing, documentation, and integration work.
The landing page requires navigation and presentation changes only; no new authentication, authorization, content-management, or visual design system is required.
RabbitMQ retry behavior is implemented in the existing Rabbit message bus and does not require changes to RabbitMQ itself or to external broker infrastructure.
Configuration values are supplied through the existing bus properties and stream deployment properties, with documented property names and validation.
The requested dependency versions are source- and binary-compatible enough that no major architectural rewrite or replacement of Spring XD subsystems is required.
Kafka consumer and producer properties can be mapped to the versions and APIs exposed by SI Kafka 1.2.0; unsupported combinations will be rejected with configuration errors.
Module and container identifiers already exist in runtime metadata or can be propagated through the current module/container launch context without redesigning deployment orchestration.
The consolidated RPM repository requires repository restructuring, build-script integration, documentation, and validation, but not creation of a new RPM packaging framework.

Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, developer-level testing, integration troubleshooting, documentation, and release/build validation, but excludes long-term maintenance and production operations.
One workday represents approximately eight hours of focused engineering effort; elapsed calendar duration and parallel staffing are not being estimated.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, message buses, web application, dependency management, runtime context, tests, CI build, and RPM repositories; identify affected APIs and establish the implementation and regression-test plan.
Implement the landing page links for sources, processors, sinks, and jobs using the existing web UI conventions; add routing/navigation tests and verify links against the deployed application.

Add bus-level and stream-deployment-level configuration for retryable and non-retryable exception types, implement precedence and cause-chain matching, handle messaging and AMQP conversion exception behavior, disable Kryo deserialization retries by default, and add configuration validation and diagnostics.

Update Spring Integration dependencies and dependency-management entries, resolve compilation and API compatibility issues, review message-channel behavior changes, and update affected tests and documentation.
Upgrade the Spring Integration Kafka extension, adapt Kafka adapter and configuration code to changed APIs, resolve transitive dependency conflicts, and execute producer/consumer compatibility tests.
Update Spring Hadoop dependencies and build metadata, resolve API or transitive dependency changes, verify Hadoop-related modules and configuration, and update regression tests.

Expose the unique module and container identifiers through the component/runtime development API or context, ensure identifiers are available during source, processor, and sink execution, and provide usage documentation and tests for logging.

activities.activity_name: Kafka bus consumer and producer default overrides
activities.activity_description: Add configurable consumer properties for autoCommitEnabled, queueSize, maxWait, and fetchSize and producer properties for batchSize and batchTimeout; map them to SI Kafka configuration, support module-level overrides over bus defaults, validate values, and test effective configuration.

activities.activity_name: Repository consolidation and RPM build scripts
activities.activity_description: Move or consolidate XD and XD-plus-Ambari RPM scripts into one public repository, preserve or document invocation changes, update build metadata and README instructions, and validate both packaging paths.

activities.activity_name: Cross-cutting dependency and build compatibility work
activities.activity_description: Resolve dependency convergence, plugin, packaging, serialization, classpath, and CI issues caused by the combined upgrades and feature changes; update generated artifacts or version metadata as required.

Create and execute focused tests for retry classification and precedence, conversion and deserialization failures, Kafka property propagation, runtime identifiers, upgraded integrations, web navigation, and representative end-to-end message flows; diagnose and fix defects found during testing.

Document new configuration properties, retry semantics, Kafka tuning options, runtime identifier access, upgrade impacts, and RPM repository usage; perform clean-build and packaging validation, update release notes, and prepare the increment for delivery.
